Grody
GROH-dee
adjective (Gen X slang)
Probably an alteration of grotesque; American teen and surfer slang from the mid-1960s, it became a Valley Girl signature in the early 1980s in the superlative grody to the max ("as disgusting as it gets"), which Moon Unit Zappa recited on "Valley Girl" (1982). The word lingers in the gross-out vocabulary of children ("that’s grody") and in Millennial nostalgia.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Grody is the Valley Girl’s word for gross — the cafeteria meatloaf, the gym socks, the creepy older guy at the arcade — and grody to the max is the top of the scale. It is a word about surfaces: what looks, smells, or feels filthy. Scripture agrees that some things are filthy, but it relocates the worst filth from the gym bag to the heart. "We are all as an unclean thing, and all our righteousnesses are as filthy rags" (Isa 64:6). Isaiah’s description of a sinful nation is grody to the max in every literal sense: "From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it; but wounds, and bruises, and putrifying sores" (Isa 1:6). The Lord said the Pharisees were like whited sepulchres, "full of dead men’s bones, and of all uncleanness" (Mat 23:27). The good news is that God does not leave the filth where He finds it. "Wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow" (Psa 51:7); "the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin" (1Jn 1:7). A child who says grody already knows two true things — that filth is real and that it ought to be washed. The gospel tells him where the worst of it is, and Who alone can wash it.

Webster 1828 Definition

Gen X / Valley Girl slang (from grotesque; "grody to the max," 1982) for gross, disgusting; Scripture locates the worst filth in the heart and its only cleansing in Christ’s blood (Isa 64:6; 1Jn 1:7).

expand to see more

GRODY, adj. (Gen X slang, 1960s surfer origin, Valley Girl peak early 1980s) Disgusting, gross, revolting. "Your locker is grody."

Grody to the max — maximally disgusting; the Valley superlative.

Probably from grotesque; companion of gag me with a spoon and barf me out.

No usable entry in Webster 1828: GROTESQUE appears there as a headword, but the transcription carries no definition; grody itself is 20th-century American slang.

Decode for parents: the word knows filth is real and should be washed — the gospel shows where the deepest filth lives and Who cleanses it.

Key Scripture

Isa 64:6 — "But we are all as an unclean thing, and all our righteousnesses are as filthy rags; and we all do fade as a leaf; and our iniquities, like the wind, have taken us away."

Isa 1:6 — "From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it; but wounds, and bruises, and putrifying sores: they have not been closed, neither bound up, neither mollified with ointment."

Mat 23:27 — "Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye are like unto whited sepulchres, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men's bones, and of all uncleanness."

Psa 51:7 — "Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean: wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow."

1Jn 1:7 — "But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin."

Modern Corruption

Grody notices filth on the surface; Scripture finds the worst of it in the heart — even in our righteousnesses — and offers the only wash that works.

expand to see more

Surface disgust, deep blindness. The teenager who recoils at a dirty locker may never be taught that pride, lust, and contempt are filthier than any gym sock. The Pharisees kept spotless exteriors over tombs full of bones (Mat 23:27). The danger is not the word but the scale it measures: a moral imagination that knows only external grossness and has no category for the uncleanness of sin.

Grody to the max, washed white. Isaiah’s catalogue of putrifying sores (Isa 1:6) is the honest diagnosis of every human heart. The Psalmist’s prayer is the honest response: "wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow" (Psa 51:7). The blood of Jesus Christ cleanses from all sin (1Jn 1:7) — not some, not the presentable sins, but all. The word that names disgust can become the doorway to the gospel.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Italian grottesca → English grotesque → 1960s surfer grody → Valley Girl grody to the max (1982); Scripture: filthy rags, washed whiter than snow (Isa 64:6; Psa 51:7).

expand to see more

Italian grottesca — cave-painting style; English grotesque — distorted, ugly

1960s California surf and teen speech: groaty / grody — gross

Early 1980s Valley Girl superlative: grody to the max

1982 "Valley Girl" single fixes it in the national ear

Biblical filth: the heart’s uncleanness (Isa 64:6); the cure: the blood of Christ (1Jn 1:7)

Usage

""Ew, the cafeteria fish sticks are grody to the max.""

"Our righteousnesses are as filthy rags (Isa 64:6) — grody, before God, to the max."

"Wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow (Psa 51:7)."
